259.t: Working with Red Allen and a band in Mexico
259.s: When Red Allen needed a band, Vincent assembled one with George Lewis and others and went to Mexico, where dance halls got rowdy.
259.q: He said Lucci used to work with Red Allen. Who? Lucci. Lucci? Lucci, Lucci. Lucci. How about Jackson? Well, Mary said, you know, when I worked with Red Allen, he had just a rockin' band, you know? And I told him if he wanted me, I'd pick him up with a band. And he told me, all right. He said,…

458.s: Beal joined Woody Herman at 19 in 1955 for about a year of one-nighters with Nat Pierce and Richie Kamuca; travel was by car and a broken-down bus, once a school bus to Newport.
458.q: Oh yeah. Yeah. It was great. Yeah I really enjoyed it. Nat Pierce was there, Richie Kamuka, you know, it was a lot of fun. Mostly one-nighters for a year. I think I was 19 when I got in that band.

787.t: Early charts, orchestration limits and leaving the road
787.s: He calls his early writing crap but says the music holds up; he couldn't hear what worked for winds, Tony Klatka helped, and he left the road in Los Angeles in 1972.
787.q: No I guess I shouldn’t say that kind of stuff but I will say this about that 20-year-old, 22, 23, is that whatever I wrote, the music holds up for me in general. I just didn’t know what I was doing in terms of orchestration and stuff. So it’s a case of if only I knew then — many times it’s the…

592.t: Auditioning for Woody Herman and going on the road
592.s: Coker auditioned in his home territory, knowing the book from listening, and treated the job as just another band.
592.q: Oh yeah. I usually like to — see when musicians would come to nearby places to be for a week or two, a lake resort, that kind of thing, I was always familiar with the lake resort, having taught, played there a lot. So it gave me a chance to see the musicians even during the day, like if they were…

678.t: Eighteen months with Woody Herman and the bus travel
678.s: He joined Woody Herman via Jake Hanna and Nat Pierce, but found the constant bus travel too rigorous; Phil Woods' joke about it.
678.ch: Woody Herman, Buddy Rich and Thad Jones
678.q: Yes, absolutely, yes. And living in New York I started going out to hear people and became friendly with people like Pepper Adams and Cecil Payne and different people. And then I spent maybe 18 months with Woody’s band. But it was very hard then. It was very rigorous. I couldn’t deal with all those…

469.t: Woody Herman's band: personnel and recommending Tony Leonardi
469.s: One-nighters by bus with Nistico, Farrell, Foster and Chase; he got Leonardi on bass.
469.q: He got very popular. So Vegas, you know. But yeah like when I was with Woody’s band it was different traveling because we did one nighters. That was rough traveling.

105.t: Not knowing Ornette's scene; leaving LA in 1947 and working 48 weeks a year
105.s: Hamilton did not know Ornette Coleman, Don Cherry or Blackwell in LA since he left in 1947; the quintet then worked 48 weeks a year with long club runs in Ohio, and he once played in Mercer Ellington's band.
105.ch: Bebop, band changes and the road
105.q: Well my quintet was in ‘55, you know, but we were in LA for about, what eight or nine months and then boom, we hit the road. Hit the road Jack. Do you know, man in those days, I stayed on the road -- we worked at least 48 weeks a year, out of the year. I mean that.

143.t: Starting his own tours, booked by Warren Stevens
143.s: He began touring from New York to California, booked partly by Warren Stevens.
143.ch: Hiatus, Blues Walk and the road
143.q: Well, I was booking a lot of the gigs, but another guy named Warren Stevens, who used to work for Ruth Bowen Booking Agency... He’s a guitar player himself. He was a good friend of mine from Columbus, Ohio. He starts booking it.

464.t: The Herbie Mann band, travel and early studio and TV work
464.s: A nine-month 1965-66 band with trombones and congas, travel stories, and then record dates and a Dick Cavett show trial.
464.ch: Studio work, Herbie Mann and recording
464.q: Sometimes we traveled in, if it was close, in Herbie’s car. I mean, not the whole band but some of the guys. The other guys have cars so we drove up to…where is that club behind the bar? Buffalo! We drove up to Buffalo, by the time we got to Albany—well, New York was, you could see the ground. By…

506.t: First tour: Jazz for Moderns with Chico Hamilton
506.s: As the new bassist on the Chico Hamilton bus, Carter focuses on learning the book with Dolphy, Budimir and Gershman.
506.q: I didn't know those guys so I was kinda by myself. But it was okay. I'd had … I didn't socialize much with anybody other than the band to find out what the library was like and how

74.t: Boston's Tick Tock and the 1949 package show
74.s: After 1948 Long Island dates he plays Boston and runs his own package show south by Greyhound.
74.ch: Package shows, Miami and the USO
74.q: And then from there we booked the Boston show--I had my own show there--
